title: MarginLab: keep the constraints visible
excerpt: Manual linear/RBF soft-margin SVM learning with replayable pair updates and editable30-feature scores.
headings: Exact feasibility before an exact bound

title: MatchLab: stable is not cost-optimal
excerpt: No pair wants to leave together. That does not select the cheapest stable assignment.

title: Personal site — midya.ca — case study
excerpt: Personal site, live at midya.ca. Built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js, deployed as a static build on DigitalOcean App Platform. The background is a procedural galaxy rendered in WebGL — nothing is loaded from outside the code: the stars, spiral galaxy, dust, constellation lines, and nebula haze are all generated at runtime.
headings: Worked example: updating the site's copy

title: MixtureLab
excerpt: Manual Gaussian-mixture EM on real, licensed chemistry. Likelihood is not identity.

title: MoeLab: mixture-of-experts from scratch, routing measured
excerpt: A mixture-of-experts layer routes each input to one (or a few) specialized sub-models instead of running one dense network over everything. MoeLab implements the whole mechanism in dependency-free Python - router, experts, sparse training objective, load-balancing term - and treats routing behavior as something to measure, not assume.
headings: MoeLab: mixture-of-experts from scratch, routing measured
Measured results (checked-in fixture, pinned in tests)
The aux-loss finding nobody puts in the README

title: OrderLab: no improving swap, still not the best order
excerpt: A strict adjacent-local optimum can still lose globally.
headings: OrderLab: no improving swap, still not the best order
Independent paths, not one echoed implementation

title: ParetoLab: the compromise a weighted sum misses
excerpt: Nondominated does not mean selected by any positive weighted sum. ParetoLab makes finite biobjective AI planning inspectable: every additive DAG path, exact scalarization interval, optimizer tie, epsilon threshold and Pareto-label pruning witness. Supplied costs, not learned preferences.
headings: ParetoLab: the compromise a weighted sum misses
Hard constraints and expectations are different problems

title: ParticleLab
excerpt: A particle filter can report equal weights and full effective sample size while carrying duplicate descendants of one badly placed initial particle. Weight ESS measures concentration of weights, not whether the state distribution has enough support. A single tidy score can hide lost uncertainty.
headings: Static square symmetry and sign loss
Retrospective paths and missing early uncertainty
Backward simulation still depends on finite support
Condition the proposal, keep the approximation honest

title: PartsLab
excerpt: Manual NumPy nonnegative matrix factorization turns original 8x8 UCI digit pixels into nonnegative additive basis contributions. A scalar-JavaScript browser solves actual new nonnegative coefficients when you edit arbitrary pixels.

title: PlanBench: the cheap run that failed
excerpt: Exact finite retry-risk analysis for supplied agent DAGs. Inspect the joint plan-success, completion-time and cost law, including exhausted retries, skip cascades and shared ancestors. A cheap failed run can satisfy a budget by skipping the work: within-limit probability is not successful-completion probability. The original seeded simulator stays unchanged.
headings: PlanBench: the cheap run that failed

title: PolicyLens: offline policy values with visible support and clipping limits
excerpt: Dependency-free Python CLI/API for standard IPS, SNIPS, DM and DR estimators. 28 tests and Python 3.10-3.13 CI; offline demo asserts exact arithmetic and a failing clipped truth-equality gate. No new statistical method.
headings: PolicyLens: offline policy values with visible support and clipping limits
Learn reward predictions without using held-out rewards

title: PPOlab
excerpt: A PPO implementation that makes reset boundaries, credit assignment and numerical replay limits inspectable.
headings: Evidence, including the failure of exact replay

title: PrivacyLab
excerpt: PrivacyLab audits supplied finite probability tables against explicit neighboring-secret edges. It computes the smallest delta at an exact multiplicative factor t=exp(epsilon), with every directed-pair event witness and full rational arithmetic. Factor 3 means epsilon ln(3), not epsilon 3.

title: PromptGuard
excerpt: An opt-in actual-scanner baseline limits how many equal-identity findings can be suppressed. One prior allowance suppresses one of three current occurrences; two remain reported, while the legacy set suppresses all three. Inspect exact path/severity identity, every before/after allowance, unused entry and gate decision.
headings: PromptGuard: an allowance is not unlimited
Retained scanner and original policy audit

title: ProvLab
excerpt: A finite relational-provenance workbench for symbolic data reasoning. Shared query variables perform real joins; projection and union-all collect derivations into natural-coefficient polynomials. The default p² + pq has bag multiplicity 10, exact answer-presence probability 1/2, and an intentionally invalid ordinary probability substitution of 3/8.
headings: ProvLab: one fact is not two chances
ProvLab0.2: same answers on every database
ProvLab0.3: the assumptions change the answer

title: QuantLab
excerpt: QuantLab now traces activation × weight integer dot products, not only packed weights. A fixed user-declared activation range produces signed 8-bit codes; every integer product and partial accumulator stays visible. Exact rational witnesses separate weight error from activation error.

title: RAGLine
excerpt: An opt-in fixed-corpus signed-vector postings backend runs the actual retrieval loop. An unvisited, implicit zero can outrank a negative match; shared-bin products can cancel to zero. Complete raw-score stable ranking stays intact before slicing and six-decimal score display.

title: RatingLab
excerpt: Observed-only rating factorization with manual NumPy alternating ridge solves, per-block decrease accounting, normal-equation residuals and full gradients. All eleven fits remain inspectable.
headings: Evaluation without hiding the stronger control
Finite response with an explicit frozen boundary

title: RectLab: a cover is not a partition
excerpt: A perfect reconstruction does not settle how its factors should be counted, or which factors are mandatory. This finite Boolean factorization inspector separates minimum overlapping covers, minimum disjoint partitions, maximal-only factor restrictions and fooling-set lower bounds. Inspect the factors, not only the headline rank.
headings: RectLab: a cover is not a partition
Version 0.2: every optimum, not only the first
A lower bound can stop short
Maximal rectangles do not preserve the census
Actual third-party reference, with its limit

title: RetrievalBench
excerpt: Exact weighted rank fusion, source prefixes and repeated votes are now inspectable end to end. An opt-in fuse-search command runs the original exhaustive BM25 index on explicitly supplied query variants, then fuses admitted prefixes using standard reciprocal rank fusion.
headings: RetrievalBench: every ranking is a vote
Corrections with the original protocol retained
